questions.question: How do you say 'hello' in French?
questions.explanation: Bonjour is the all-purpose greeting in French, used from morning until early evening; after that, switch to bonsoir (good evening).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bonjour means hello.

questions.question: What does 'merci' mean in English?
questions.explanation: Merci is how you thank someone; the common reply is de rien (you're welcome).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Merci means thank you.

questions.question: How do you say 'goodbye' in French?
questions.explanation: Au revoir is the standard goodbye for any time of day; bonsoir is a greeting, not a farewell.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Au revoir means goodbye.

questions.question: What does 'la maison' mean?
questions.explanation: La maison is feminine, so it takes la; contrast la maison (house) with l'appartement (apartment).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: La maison is the house.

questions.question: What does 'le chien' mean?
questions.explanation: Le chien is masculine, so it takes le; the feminine form is la chienne.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Le chien is the dog.

questions.question: What does 'l'école' mean?
questions.explanation: École starts with a vowel sound, so la becomes l': l'école. The noun is still feminine.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: L'école is the school.

questions.question: How do you say 'water' in French?
questions.explanation: Eau is feminine but starts with a vowel, so it becomes l'eau; un verre d'eau is a glass of water.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: L'eau is water.

questions.question: What does 'rouge' mean?
questions.explanation: Rouge comes after the noun it describes: une pomme rouge, a red apple.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rouge is red.

questions.question: What does 'grand' mean?
questions.explanation: Grand describes size: for things it means big or large (une grande maison), and for people it means tall (un homme grand).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Grand means big.

questions.question: How do you say 'friend' in French?
questions.explanation: Ami means friend; amie is the feminine form.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ami is friend.

questions.question: What does 'la famille' mean?
questions.explanation: Famille is feminine: la famille. Related words: le père (father), la mère (mother).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: La famille is the family.

questions.question: What does 'aujourd'hui' mean?
questions.explanation: Aujourd'hui is a single fixed word for today; hier is yesterday and demain is tomorrow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Aujourd'hui is today.

questions.question: How do you say 'Monday' in French?
questions.explanation: French days of the week are not capitalized: lundi, mardi, mercredi. Lundi is Monday.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lundi is Monday.

questions.question: What does 'le livre' mean?
questions.explanation: Livre is masculine: le livre. Watch out: la livre is a different word meaning a pound (weight).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Le livre is the book.

questions.question: What does 'manger' mean?
questions.explanation: Manger is a regular -er verb: je mange, tu manges. It keeps a soft g before a and o: nous mangeons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Manger is to eat.

questions.question: What does 'boire' mean?
questions.explanation: Boire is irregular: je bois, nous buvons. Do not confuse it with manger (to eat).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Boire is to drink.

questions.question: How do you say 'thank you very much' in French?
questions.explanation: Beaucoup means a lot or very much, so merci beaucoup is a stronger thank-you than merci alone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Merci beaucoup means thanks a lot.

questions.question: What does 'la table' mean?
questions.explanation: Table is feminine: la table. Most nouns ending in -e are feminine, though there are exceptions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: La table is the table.

questions.question: What does 'heureux' mean?
questions.explanation: Heureux is the masculine form; the feminine is heureuse. It describes a feeling, so it is used with être: je suis heureux.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Heureux is happy.

questions.question: How do you say 'I love you' in French?
questions.explanation: Je t'aime puts the object pronoun te before the verb: je t'aime, I love you.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je t'aime means I love you.

questions.question: What does 'la ville' mean?
questions.explanation: La ville is the standard word for a city (une grande ville, a big city); un village is a village and la campagne is the countryside.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: La ville is the city.

questions.question: What does 'le train' mean?
questions.explanation: Train is masculine: le train. Related travel words: la gare (station), le billet (ticket).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Le train is the train.

questions.question: What does 'la fenêtre' mean?
questions.explanation: Fenêtre is feminine: la fenêtre. The ê in French often marks a lost historical s (compare the old spelling fenestre).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: La fenêtre is the window.

questions.question: What does 'vite' mean?
questions.explanation: Vite is an adverb meaning fast or quickly: cours vite! (run fast!). The adjective for fast is rapide.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vite means fast.

questions.question: What does 'les devoirs' mean?
questions.explanation: Devoirs is almost always plural for homework: les devoirs. The singular le devoir means a duty.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Les devoirs is homework.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'parler' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: For -er verbs, the je form ends in -e: je parle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je parle, I speak.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'manger' for 'tu'?
questions.explanation: For -er verbs, the tu form ends in -es: tu manges.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu manges, you eat.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'finir' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: For -ir verbs, the il form ends in -it: il finit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il finit, he finishes.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'parler' for 'nous'?
questions.explanation: For -er verbs, the nous form ends in -ons: nous parlons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nous parlons, we speak.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'finir' for 'ils'?
questions.explanation: For -ir verbs, the ils form ends in -issent: ils finissent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ils finissent, they finish.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'être' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Être is the most irregular French verb; its present forms are je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont - learn them by heart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je suis, I am.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'aller' for 'nous'?
questions.explanation: Aller is irregular, and its nous form is allons: nous allons au parc (we are going to the park).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nous allons, we go.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'avoir' for 'tu'?
questions.explanation: Avoir present forms: j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont. Tu as keeps the s that il a drops.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu as, you have.

questions.question: What does 'être' mean, and when is it used?
questions.correctAnswer: To be, for identity, traits, and origin
distractors: To be, for temporary feelings only
questions.explanation: Use être to say what someone or something IS: identity (c'est un professeur), description (elle est grande), origin (nous sommes de Paris) and profession (il est médecin, with no article).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Être is for what something is.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'faire' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Faire present: je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font. The singular forms fais/fais/fait are pronounced the same.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il fait, he does or makes.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Marie ___ à l'école.'
questions.explanation: Location uses être: Marie est à l'école.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Être is used for location.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Ils ___ étudiants.'
questions.explanation: After être, professions take no article: ils sont étudiants (they are students), not des étudiants.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ils sont means they are.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'vouloir' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Vouloir present: je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent. The je and tu forms end in -x.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je veux, I want.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'pouvoir' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Pouvoir follows the same pattern as vouloir: je peux, tu peux, il peut. Both verbs switch to a -t ending for il.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il peut, he can.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'dormir' for 'nous'?
questions.explanation: Dormir belongs to the -mir family (dormir, partir, sortir): the singular drops the last stem consonant - je dors, tu dors, il dort - but nous dormons keeps it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nous dormons, we sleep.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'venir' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Venir present: je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent. The same viend- pattern appears in tenir.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je viens, I come.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'savoir' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Savoir present: je sais, tu sais, il sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils savent. The je/tu forms end in -s, not -x like vouloir.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je sais, I know.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'dire' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Dire present: je dis, tu dis, il dit, nous disons, vous dites, ils disent. The vous form dites is irregular - it is not built on the dis- stem.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il dit, he says.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'voir' for 'tu'?
questions.explanation: Voir present: je vois, tu vois, il voit, nous voyons, vous voyez, ils voient. Note the y in the nous and vous forms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu vois, you see.

questions.question: What is the correct present tense form of 'prendre' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Prendre present: je prends, tu prends, il prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent. The je/tu forms keep the d and add s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je prends, I take.

questions.question: What does 'j'aime' mean?
questions.explanation: Aimer covers both like and love; context decides. For people, aimer means love; for things and activities, it usually means like.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: J'aime means I like.

questions.question: How do you say 'I like the books' in French?
questions.explanation: J'aime les livres: les livres is plural, so use les.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: J'aime les livres means I like the books.

questions.question: What is the correct form: 'Tu ___ le football.'
questions.explanation: Aimer is a regular -er verb, so the tu form takes -es: tu aimes. The s is silent but required in writing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu aimes means you like.

questions.question: What is the present tense form of 'être' for 'vous'?
questions.explanation: Être present: vous êtes. The circumflex in êtes is required - etes is not a correct French spelling.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Vous êtes, you are.

questions.question: What is the present tense form of 'avoir' for 'ils'?
questions.explanation: Avoir present: ils ont. Do not confuse ont (they have) with sont (they are).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ils ont, they have.

questions.question: What is the passé composé used for?
questions.explanation: The passé composé tells what happened at a specific completed moment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Passé composé is for what happened, done.

questions.question: What is the passé composé of 'parler' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Passé composé uses avoir plus the past participle: j'ai parlé.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: J'ai parlé means I spoke.

questions.question: What is the passé composé of 'manger' for 'elle'?
questions.explanation: The passé composé of manger is auxiliary avoir (elle a) plus the past participle mangé; regular -er verbs form the participle in -é.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Elle a mangé means she ate.

questions.question: What is the passé composé of 'aller' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: Aller uses être in the passé composé: je suis allé.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je suis allé means I went.

questions.question: What is the passé composé of 'venir' for 'ils'?
questions.explanation: Venir uses être: ils sont venus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ils sont venus means they came.

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'finir'?
questions.explanation: The past participle of -ir verbs ends in -i: fini.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fini is the past participle of finir.

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'prendre'?
questions.explanation: Prendre has the irregular past participle pris.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pris is the past participle of prendre.

questions.question: What is the imparfait used for?
questions.correctAnswer: Ongoing or repeated past actions and descriptions
questions.explanation: The imparfait describes what was happening or used to happen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Imparfait is for what was going on.

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'parler' for 'tu'?
questions.explanation: The imparfait tu form of -er verbs ends in -ais: tu parlais.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu parlais means you were speaking.

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'etre' for 'nous'?
questions.explanation: The imparfait of être uses the stem ét-: nous étions, vous étiez. Être is the only verb whose imparfait stem does not come from its nous present form.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nous étions means we were.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Hier, je ___ à l'école.'
questions.explanation: Hier (yesterday) with a completed action takes the passé composé: je suis allé.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hier plus a finished action is passé composé.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Quand j'étais petit, je ___ beaucoup.'
questions.explanation: Quand j'étais petit describes a repeated past habit, so use the imparfait: jouais.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Used to play is imparfait.

questions.question: What is the passe compose of 'faire' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Faire has the irregular past participle fait: il a fait. It must be memorized - there is no regular -ait rule.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il a fait means he did or made.

questions.question: What is the passe compose of 'dire' for 'elles'?
questions.explanation: Dire has the past participle dit: elles ont dit. Like fait, dit is a short irregular participle to memorize.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Elles ont dit means they said.

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'aller' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: In the imparfait, aller is regular: the stem all- plus imparfait endings gives j'allais. Its passé composé is the irregular one (je suis allé).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: J'allais means I was going.

questions.question: What is the passe compose of 'voir' for 'tu'?
questions.explanation: Voir has the past participle vu: tu as vu. Short -u participles are common: bu (drunk), lu (read), pu (been able to).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tu as vu means you saw.

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'vivre' for 'ils'?
questions.explanation: Vivre in the imparfait: the stem viv- plus -aient gives ils vivaient, for an ongoing past situation (they were living, they used to live).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ils vivaient means they were living.

questions.question: What is the passe compose of 'écrire' for 'nous'?
questions.explanation: Écrire has the past participle écrit: nous avons écrit. Its present stem changes too: nous écrivons, with é.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nous avons écrit means we wrote.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Pendant que je cuisinais, il ___ la table.'
questions.explanation: A completed action interrupting an ongoing one takes the passe compose: il a mis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The interruption is passe compose.

questions.question: What is the imparfait of 'avoir' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Avoir in the imparfait uses the stem av-: il avait. The same verb has the future stem aur- (il aura).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il avait means he had.

questions.question: What is the futur simple of 'parler' for 'je'?
questions.explanation: The futur simple adds -ai to the infinitive for je: je parlerai.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Je parlerai means I will speak.

questions.question: What is the futur simple of 'avoir' for 'il'?
questions.explanation: Avoir has an irregular future stem, aur-: il aura, nous aurons. Many common verbs change their stem in the future: être gives ser-, aller gives ir-.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Il aura means he will have.

questions.question: How do you give a formal command for 'parler' to 'vous'?
questions.explanation: The vous command uses the vous present form: parlez.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Parlez is the polite command.

questions.question: How do you give an informal command for 'manger' to 'tu'?
questions.explanation: The tu affirmative command drops the final s: mange.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mange means eat, as a command.

questions.question: What is the direct object pronoun for 'le livre'?
questions.explanation: Le livre is masculine singular, so its direct object pronoun is le.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Le replaces a masculine singular thing.

questions.question: What is the indirect object pronoun for 'à Marie'?
questions.explanation: À Marie is the recipient, so use the indirect object pronoun lui.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lui means to her or to him.

questions.question: Which adjective agrees with 'les maisons'?
questions.explanation: Les maisons is feminine plural, so the adjective is belles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adjectives match the noun in gender and number.

questions.question: Where does the adjective usually go in French?
distractors: At the start of the sentence
questions.explanation: In French, most descriptive adjectives follow the noun: maison blanche.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In French the adjective usually follows the noun.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'savoir' and 'connaître'?
questions.correctAnswer: Savoir is knowing facts; connaître is knowing people or places
questions.explanation: Savoir is to know information; connaître is to be familiar with people or places.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Savoir is facts, connaître is familiarity.

questions.question: What is the comparative form for 'taller': 'Marie est ___ grande que Anne.'
questions.explanation: Comparisons use plus... que (more... than), moins... que (less... than) and aussi... que (as... as). This sentence says taller, so the word is plus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plus means more.

questions.question: What is the superlative for 'most interesting': 'C'est le livre ___ intéressant de tous.'
questions.explanation: The superlative is le/la/les plus + adjective: le livre le plus intéressant de tous, the most interesting book of all.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Le plus means the most.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been France's capital for centuries; it is also the country's largest city and sits on the river Seine.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Paris is France's capital.

questions.question: What is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.correctAnswer: A famous iron tower in Paris built for the 1889 World's Fair
distractors: A castle in the Loire Valley
questions.explanation: The Eiffel Tower was built in Paris for the 1889 Exposition Universelle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 fair.

questions.question: What is the currency of France?
questions.explanation: France adopted the euro in 2002, replacing the franc - which is why the franc is the trap answer here.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: France's money is the euro.

questions.question: What is 'la Bastille' associated with?
questions.correctAnswer: The French Revolution, stormed on July 14, 1789
questions.explanation: The storming of the Bastille in 1789 began the French Revolution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Bastille fell on July 14, 1789.

questions.question: Which French artist painted the water lilies?
questions.explanation: Monet painted his famous water lilies series at Giverny.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Monet painted water lilies at Giverny.

questions.question: What is a croissant?
distractors: A type of bread only for breakfast in Italy
questions.explanation: Croissant means crescent in French; the pastry is named for its crescent shape and made from laminated, butter-layered dough.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A croissant is a flaky butter pastry.

questions.question: What does 'bonsoir' mean?
questions.explanation: Bonsoir is the evening greeting, used from about 6 p.m.; bonne nuit is reserved for when someone is going to bed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bonsoir is good evening.

questions.question: What does 'à demain' mean?
questions.explanation: Demain means tomorrow, so à demain is the natural parting phrase: see you tomorrow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: À demain is see you tomorrow.

questions.question: What is the correct question word for 'where'?
questions.explanation: Où with a grave accent means where; without the accent, ou means or. The accent changes the word completely.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Où is where.

questions.question: What is the correct question word for 'why'?
questions.explanation: Pourquoi asks for a reason; the typical answer begins with parce que (because).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pourquoi is why.

questions.question: What is the correct question word for 'when'?
questions.explanation: Quand asks when; do not confuse it with comment (how) or combien (how much, how many).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Quand is when.

questions.question: What is the correct question word for 'how'?
questions.explanation: Comment asks how or what something is like: comment ça va? (how is it going?).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Comment is how.

questions.question: What is the correct question word for 'who'?
questions.explanation: Qui asks who and can be the subject or the object: qui est là? (who is there?).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Qui is who.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am 15 years old' in French?
questions.explanation: Age uses avoir: j'ai quinze ans.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Age uses avoir in French.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'le journal'?
questions.explanation: Journal becomes journaux in the plural, an irregular -al to -aux change.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Journal becomes journaux.

questions.question: What does 's'il vous plaît' mean?
questions.explanation: S'il vous plaît is the polite way to say please.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: S'il vous plaît means please.

questions.question: What does 'de rien' mean?
questions.explanation: De rien is a common reply to merci.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: De rien means you're welcome.

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'beau'?
questions.explanation: Beau becomes belle in the feminine singular.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Beau becomes belle.

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'nouveau'?
questions.explanation: Nouveau becomes nouvelle in the feminine singular.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nouveau becomes nouvelle.
